Tracking the Enemy Jungler

Most early deaths come from the enemy jungler. Learn to guess where they are, so you know when to play safe and when to go for it.

Why tracking matters

The enemy jungler is the biggest threat to your lane in the first 15 minutes. If you know they're on the other side of the map, you can trade, push and play aggressive without fear. If you think they might be close, you play safe and stay near your tower.

You can't see the jungler most of the time, but you can make good guesses from a few clues. Strong players do this constantly, and it's one of the biggest differences between climbing and staying stuck.

Camp spawns and the first clear

Jungle camps spawn early in 2026:

CampFirst spawnRespawn
Blue Sentinel, Red Brambleback0:555:00
Murk Wolves, Raptors0:552:15
Gromp, Krugs1:072:15
Rift Scuttler2:552:30

Most junglers start at one buff (red or blue) and clear the camps on that side of the map, then either gank the closest lane or continue to the other side. A full clear of six camps usually finishes a little after 3:00. That means a jungler who started bottom side often shows up top side around 3:00, and the other way round.

Pro tipLook at which of your laners doesn't get a leash, or watch where the enemy jungler appears on your wards at the start. If they started bot side, the top side of the map is where they'll likely be next.

Clues to look for

  • Where they were last seen. If the enemy jungler shows up in bot lane at 3:30, they can't be top at 3:40. Use that window to trade hard.
  • Missing camps. When you walk through the enemy jungle and a camp is gone, the jungler was there recently.
  • Scuttle crab. Scuttle spawns at 2:55. If the enemy jungler is fighting for it, they're in the river.
  • Lane behavior. If your opponent suddenly walks forward and plays aggressive, the jungler is probably close.
  • Objectives. Around 5:00 (dragon) and 8:00 (grubs), junglers move toward those pits.

Play safe or aggressive?

Every few seconds, ask: "Where could the enemy jungler be?" Then choose:

  • Jungler seen on the other side of the map: this is your chance. Trade, push, take plates or go for a kill.
  • Jungler unknown: play carefully. Don't walk far up the lane without vision, and keep an escape ready.
  • Jungler likely near your lane: stay near your tower, let the wave come to you, and don't use Flash on a risky trade.

Your own jungler matters too. If both junglers are on your side of the map, a fight might break out. Being ready to help (with your wave pushed) can win a 2v2.

Common mistakePushing all the way up the lane with no wards when the enemy jungler hasn't been seen for a while. This is the most common way to die to a gank.

Warding for the jungler

Wards are your eyes on the jungler. Some good timings:

  • Around 2:45-3:00: ward the river or jungle entrance near your lane. This is when the first ganks usually happen after a full clear.
  • After every recall: place a ward on the way back.
  • Before objectives: ward near the pit about a minute before it spawns.

Your Stealth Ward trinket has 2 charges. Use them, don't save them. Each player can have 3 Stealth Wards and 1 Control Ward on the map. For more, see Vision Basics: Wards and the Minimap and Advanced Vision Control.

Using the minimap

None of this works without looking at the minimap. Get into the habit of glancing at it every few seconds, especially after every last hit. Over time it becomes automatic.

When you spot the enemy jungler, ping their location so your team knows. A well-timed ping can save a teammate's life and lets the whole team play more aggressively on the safe side of the map. See Teamwork, Pings and Role Quests.

Key takeaways

  • Camps spawn at 0:55 (Gromp and Krugs at 1:07). A full clear ends a little after 3:00.
  • A jungler who started on one side often shows up on the other side around 3:00.
  • When the enemy jungler is seen far away, play aggressive. When unknown, play careful.
  • Ward the river around 3:00, after every recall, and before objectives.
  • Look at the minimap after every last hit, and ping the jungler when you see them.
